title: Defensive overnight-capture sleeve: close-to-open exposure on a defensive book, with the intraday leg as causal control (overnight-vs-intraday return decomposition)
outcome_blind_attestation: Proposal written before any scored window exists. No candidate returns, PF, Sharpe or rankings were computed, and no other proposal lane's files were read. Literature expectations are qualitative priors only.

economic_mechanism.statement: US equity expected returns are earned at different times of the session: documented US evidence shows the average equity premium accrues disproportionately to holding overnight (regular-session close to next regular-session open), while the average intraday (open-to-close) return is near zero or negative for the broad market. The mechanism generating this localization is institutional infrequent rebalancing: investors who trade occasionally accumulate/distribute around session-boundary auctions, transferring overnight exposure to whoever holds through the close and concentrating intraday price pressure on those who trade during sessions. The family holds a defensive (low-beta) long book only overnight - entered at the closing auction, exited at the next opening auction - capturing the overnight component while refusing the intraday component of the same names.
economic_mechanism.counterparty: Intraday-horizon traders and flow-driven institutions whose rebalancing pressure is concentrated in session-boundary auctions (the infrequent-rebalancing cohorts of Bogousslavsky 2016); also investors structurally averse to holding overnight-gap risk who demand to be compensated for it. We are the overnight-exposure provider on the other side of their intraday-flat preference.
economic_mechanism.why_the_edge_exists: The overnight/intraday split is not priced like a single daily return: French-Roll (1986) show variance and information processing are concentrated in sessions; Lou-Polk-Skouras (2019) show premia localize into overnight vs intraday components by ownership/strategy clienteles. Compensating holders for overnight gap risk, with buying pressure concentrated at the close, produces a persistent positive overnight average that naive daily-close bars average together with a negative intraday average.

literature.citation: French, K. and R. Roll (1986), 'Stock Return Variances: The Arrival of Information and the Reaction of Traders', Journal of Financial Economics 17(1).
literature.claim_used: Return variance and price discovery concentrate in trading hours; non-trading intervals (overnight, weekends, holidays) are structurally distinct return states.

literature.citation: Lou, D., C. Polk and S. Skouras (2019), 'A Tug of War: Overnight Versus Intraday Expected Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 134(1).
literature.claim_used: US equities' expected returns decompose into overnight and intraday components with opposite signs on average; the overnight component is positive for broad/defensive/quality-like books while intraday is negative on average.

literature.citation: Bogousslavsky, V. (2016), 'Infrequent Rebalancing, Return Autocorrelation, and Seasonality', Journal of Finance 71(6).
literature.claim_used: Infrequently rebalancing institutions concentrate order flow near session boundaries, generating overnight-momentum/intraday-reversal patterns - the mechanism behind overnight localization.

literature.citation: Aboody, D., O. Even-Tov, R. Lehavy and B. Trueman (2018), 'Overnight Returns and Firm-Specific Investor Sentiment', Journal of Financial Economics 127(2).
literature.claim_used: Overnight-vs-intraday asymmetry varies cross-sectionally with clientele/sentiment; grounds the ownership-conditioned neighbour.

universe_neutralization_benchmark.universe: PIT-accepted liquid US common stocks/ETFs from A3 (>= 30 eligible names per decision), filtered to the low-beta defensive subset defined below.
universe_neutralization_benchmark.neutralization: Defensive context: long-only book equal/sector-capped weighted across the bottom-beta tercile (252-session rolling beta vs SPY, PIT), with sector caps so the book is not a single-sector bond-proxy. No short leg in the anchor/control (the mechanism is an exposure-selection sleeve, not a cross-sectional ranking bet).
universe_neutralization_benchmark.benchmark: Flat (cash) and SPY total return; declared factor-neutral context: market-beta-matched overnight exposure (book beta reported against SPY so the sleeve is interpretable as a partial-market-exposure overlay), sector-capped.

clocks.formation_clock: Calendar-anchored (no signal event): the book is re-derived each session from the previous close's PIT beta tercile membership; formation decisions are computed from data strictly before the entry instant.
clocks.holding_clock: Overnight interval only: buy at session_bounds(day).end_utc (closing auction; 13:00 ET on early closes), hold the overnight gap, sell at next_session(day).start_utc (opening auction). The interval spans weekends, holidays and the 13:00 early-close boundaries exactly as the frozen table declares; the pre-holiday overnight (e.g., the ~41h Thanksgiving eve interval) is a structurally longer overnight state, not a missing bar.
clocks.execution_clock: Double-auction execution: closing auction entry, next opening auction exit. Gaps between are classified by classify_gap as GAP_OK_WITH_REASON (outside regular sessions; the gap IS the return). A name halted through the exit open (declared HaltInterval) is carried to the first halt-free open - no synthetic fill ever; an unexplained in-session gap fails closed and stops the book for that name.
clocks.calendar_expressibility: Fully session-calendar native: session_bounds, next_session, early_close_cutoff_utc; baseline scoring keeps pre/post phases disabled - the overnight return is the close-to-open gap between regular sessions, NOT a pre/post-market strategy. The calendar manifest digest is part of the trial identity.

turnover_capacity.expected_turnover: Literature-informed prior, not a computed result: full-notional daily round trip at session boundaries (100% one-sided turnover per session day, ~250 round trips/year), the highest-turnover shape of any family in this sprint; capacity therefore hinges on auction liquidity of the defensive mega-cap subset.
turnover_capacity.expected_capacity: Low eight figures USD at <= 5% of closing/opening auction volume in low-beta large caps; auction participation beyond that moves the close against the book, directly consuming the overnight premium.
turnover_capacity.cost_sensitivity_declared: This family lives or dies on double-auction costs: the S6 x1.5 commission/spread stress and the declared auction-cost proxy are gates by construction; the proposal accepts the risk that auction costs make it infeasible - that is an honest null, not a hidden grid.

arms.name: anchor_overnight_lowbeta
arms.definition: Long defensive book (bottom-beta tercile, sector-capped, PIT) bought at the closing auction, sold at the next opening auction, every session day including early closes and holiday-spanning intervals.
arms.role: Captures the documented positive overnight component of the same names' returns.

arms.name: neighbour_overnight_high_own
arms.definition: Identical overnight clock, but the book is selected by high PIT institutional ownership (13F, with filing-lag availability dates) instead of low beta.
arms.role: Theoretically justified neighbour: Lou-Polk-Skouras (2019) attribute overnight localization to ownership clienteles - the mechanism's state variable - so the same clock applied to the ownership-selected book should also capture the overnight premium. Supports the anchor if the mechanism is clientele-driven overnight compensation rather than low-beta per se.

arms.name: control_intraday_lowbeta
arms.definition: The identical anchor book, but held intraday only: bought at the opening auction, sold at the same session's closing auction, flat overnight.
arms.role: Causal negative control: same names, same formation, same trading frequency, only the holding interval differs. The mechanism predicts the overnight premium vanishes here (US evidence: average intraday component ~zero or negative), so a materially weaker/destructive control isolates the overnight interval - the calendar's close-to-open gap - as the causal carrier. If intraday matches overnight, the family is falsified: the edge would be plain market beta.

corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.corporate_actions: Splits/cash dividends applied exactly once at ex/effective timestamps (default: ex-date open). When the exit open coincides with an ex-date, the position held through the prior close is entitled: the engine accrues cash_to_position at the ex/effective moment and the raw-vs-total-return reconciliation must close at that boundary. Signals/beta on the TOTAL_RETURN path; auction fills on the RAW path.
corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.earnings: No earnings conditioning: names are held regardless of their announcement calendar, which is what makes this family's information set disjoint from A4 Family 1 (PEAD). Earnings-day overnight gaps are simply part of the overnight return stream.
corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.borrow: No short legs in any arm; borrow treatment is 'not required', declared explicitly so the SD4 borrow gates trivially but honestly (no free-borrow assumptions anywhere).
corporate_action_earnings_borrow_dividen.dividends: Long legs receive cash dividends; the dividend yield lands in the overnight leg whenever ex-dates follow holds, and the SPY total-return benchmark keeps dividend treatment symmetric.

falsification_rule.pre_registered: Family survives only if (a) anchor: after-cost expectancy > 0 and position PF >= 1.10 with >= 2/3 chronological folds positive and no fold PF < 0.80 (PLAN section 13); (b) neighbour supports anchor (positive overnight premium, same sign); (c) intraday-only control destroys or materially weakens the effect (intraday expectancy <= overnight expectancy by an economically declared margin; intraday expectancy <= 0 is the mechanism's point prediction); (d) drop-one-symbol/sector/fold survival and the S6 auction-cost stress hold. If the control matches the anchor, the family is rejected: it was market beta wearing a calendar costume.
external_validity_caveats: The positive-average overnight component is strongest in US large caps in recent decades and is regime-dependent; prior decades and other markets differ, so a null on S0 is a legitimate outcome.
Double-auction costs are the dominant feasibility risk; small changes in the declared auction-cost proxy can flip net expectancy (cost-gate honesty is declared up front).

Open/close print quality decides the decomposition: consolidated fields contaminated by after-hours prints silently fake or destroy the overnight return; provider print-at-bounds verification is mandatory before real scoring.
Early closes and holiday-spanning overnights are structurally different intervals; the frozen 2027-2030 calendar entries are rule-derived pending provider verification.
Beta and ownership inputs are PIT-lagged estimators; estimation-window drift changes the book and therefore the trial identity.

novelty_defense.vs_rejected_crypto_families: Not a rescue of weekly reversal: the observable is the session-decomposed close-to-open return capture (not a weekly reversal score), the counterparty is auction-concentrated infrequent rebalancers/intraday-flat investors, the clock is daily double-auction on the NYSE session calendar with early-close and holiday-spanning intervals (no weekly calendar anywhere), and the causal control is the intraday-only leg of the same book (not a shuffled or inverted reversal signal). Not M01 aggressor-flow absorption (no order-flow imbalance observable, no L2/microstructure inputs) and not funding-carry (no funding cashflows; US cash equities only).
novelty_defense.vs_A4_family1_PEAD: Different observable (return decomposition vs accounting surprise), different conditioning (pure calendar clock vs event-anchored timestamps), different counterparty, different control (intraday leg vs sign-flipped surprise), disjoint information sets (no earnings data used).
novelty_defense.lens_note: The edge lives exactly where naive session handling silently fakes or destroys the effect: daily-bar pipelines average the overnight and intraday components into one close-to-close return; DST-correct UTC bounds, 13:00 early closes, holiday-spanning gaps and halt fail-closed semantics are the difference between measuring and inventing this premium.
